basis: Tootsie Roll’s May 9 Form 10-Q establishes that consolidated GAAP revenue for the quarter ended March 31, 2024 was $153,175,000 versus $162,092,000 a year earlier. That is a 5.50% decline and $812,400 below the $153,987,400 cutoff. The April 24 release disclosed only the product-sales component. The remaining gap is the May 6 annual shareholder meeting. The proxy and voting report establish that the meeting occurred, but I could not verify what financial figures management presented or distributed. May 9 is the earliest qualifying document I could verify. The earliest public disclosure date remains unresolved.

coverage.detail: October 25, 2023 Q3 release. Management expected earlier Halloween shipments to weigh on Q4 2023 sales relative to Q4 2022. It gave no numeric Q1 2024 revenue outlook.
February 16, 2024 Q4 release. The $195,368,000 sales figure covers Q4 2023. Management expected supply-chain conditions to improve through 2024 and gave no Q1 2024 revenue ceiling.
The year-end Form 10-K referred to Q1 2024 as the expected completion period for Canadian labor negotiations. It supplied no quarterly revenue bound.
The 2023 annual report distributed with the proxy materials reviewed full-year product sales and pricing. I found no numeric Q1 2024 consolidated revenue outlook.

April 24 Q1 release. Its table identifies $151,464,000 and $160,711,000 as net product sales for Q1 2024 and Q1 2023. For the 2024 total to meet the cutoff, rental and royalty revenue had to be at most $2,523,400. The release gave neither that component’s amount nor an upper bound.
Item 2.02 confirms the company issued the earnings release on April 24 for the quarter ended March 31. It incorporates the same exhibit.

The issuer’s proxy on its designated materials host scheduled the May 6 meeting for noon EDT at One James Center, Suite 200, Richmond, Virginia. The agenda covered directors, auditor ratification and other business. The notice supplied no webcast or replay address.
The 2024 proxy card identifies the materials portal and gives voting instructions. It contains no record of the meeting proceedings.

I reopened the host portal and followed all three visible materials links. https://www.astproxyportal.com/ast/14960/Download returned 404, https://www.astproxyportal.com/ast/14960/Print returned 403, and https://www.astproxyportal.com/ast/14960/Request%20Materials returned 404. None yielded a deck, transcript or audio.
The historical portal lookup was inaccessible. Its meeting-day contents remain unverified.

I followed the issuer’s Company Financials link and searched outside EDGAR for Q1 preliminary results, updated guidance, investor presentations, earnings calls and May 6 remarks. The accessible archive page exposed no event materials. The searches yielded no official recording, transcript or full deck covering the gap.
The May 10 voting report confirms the May 6 meeting occurred and reports director elections and auditor ratification. It gives no account of financial remarks.
The meeting filing’s exhibit inventory contains no presentation, transcript or EX-99.

The EDGAR earnings table confirms both March quarters on the same consolidated basis. In 2024, $151,464,000 of product sales plus $1,711,000 of rental and royalty revenue totaled $153,175,000. In 2023, $160,711,000 plus $1,381,000 totaled $162,092,000.
The issuer-hosted Q1 Form 10-Q provides the same consolidated statement on page 5. I could not establish an earlier public posting date for this copy.
EDGAR records the March 31 Form 10-Q as filed May 9, 2024 and accepted at 15:00:40 that day.

publication_date_evidence: The April 24 exhibit is marked for immediate release, and the accompanying 8-K confirms issuance that day. EDGAR’s May 9 acceptance timestamps the consolidated actual used for upper_bound. The available May 6 meeting records establish the event date but leave the content of management’s remarks and handouts unresolved.
